prerequisites: It is recommended to have at least partially achieved the learning objectives established in the following second-year subjects: Technologies and Programming Paradigms, Human-Computer Interaction, and Databases.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to design, develop, select and evaluate applications, ensuring their reliability, security and quality, in accordance with ethical principles and current legislation and regulations.
Ability to plan, conceive, deploy and manage IT projects, services and systems in all areas, leading their implementation and continuous improvement and assessing their economic and social impact.
Ability to understand the importance of negotiation, effective work habits, leadership and communication skills in all software development environments.
Knowledge and application of software engineering principles, methodologies and life cycles.
Analyze and elaborate the different models that make up the functional specification of a software system starting from given requirements.
Elaborate the technical design of a software system according to a specification.
Design and execute tests on the components of a software system.
Review and evaluate the specification and design of a software system.
Elaborate the development and implementation plan for an application.
Negotiate with the client the requirements and implementation deadlines for an application.
Make technical presentations of the different products elaborated during the development of a software system.
Participate in a team for the elaboration of the specification and design of a software system.
Understand the specific problems of software projects in relation to other types of engineering projects.
Apply a methodology for defining a software system.
Know different approaches and methodologies for software development.
Know the main national and international standards for software development.

syllabus_topics: General problems and characteristics of software

assessment_methods.method: Practical assignments (team and individual work, oral presentation, results)

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in each part (theory and practicals). If this requirement is met, the final grade is the weighted average (50% each part). Otherwise, the final grade is the weighted average with a maximum of 4 points. For extraordinary calls, theory and practical grades from the ordinary call are used if they were at least 5 out of 10; otherwise, these parts are re-evaluated by an exam or individual assignment respectively. A minimum of 5 out of 10 points is required in each part. If met, the final grade is the weighted average (50% each part); otherwise, the final grade is the weighted average with a maximum of 4 points. For differentiated evaluation, both theory and practical parts are assessed by an exam and an individual assignment respectively, with the same minimum score and weighting rules as extraordinary calls.
